The Petitioners are seeking approval of the Commission on the Tender documents that have been prepared in accordance with the above-mentioned guidelines. 8. The Petitioners have also submitted the details such as eligibility criteria for bidders, selection process of bidders, letter of awards and signing of agreements, etc., as prescribed in the Tender document. 12. Learned counsel of the Petitioners submitted that the details of deviations proposed to be made, along with the rationale thereof, have been furnished in the Petition, and the Petitioners are also praying for permission to initiate the bidding process i.e., to float the tender incorporating the proposed deviations, which shall be subject to the approval of the Commission. 13. After hearing the Petitioners, the Commission observed that the Petitioners have inter alia also prayed for approval of the tender documents, which prima facie, appeared to be beyond the scope of Part A - Clause 5.1 of the Guidelines, which requires the prior approval of the Appropriate Commission only for deviation from the process defined in the Guidelines before the initiation of the bidding process and not to the tender document itself. Accordingly, the Commission admitted the Petition subject to just exceptions. Also, the 27/IA/2025 (Diary) No. 433/2025 filed for the early listing of the Petition, having served its purpose, was disposed of. 14. The Commission also issued a public notice on 07.10.2025 to seek comments from the stakeholders on the petition. 16. The Petitioners submitted additional information to place on record the comments received from various stakeholders, response to their queries, deviations from the Tariff-Based Competitive Bidding Guidelines dated 06.02.2025, amendments in the Tender and amendments in the PSPPA carried out by the Petitioners. Following the issuance of the Public Notice on 07.10.2025, various industry stakeholders, including Adani, Renew, Tata, Sanga mam, Torrent, Avaada, and SPDA, submitted their queries and suggestions regarding the Tender Documents. The Petitioners subsequently filed an additional affidavit dated 15.01.2026, placing on record their technical rebuttals, responses, and the finalised list of deviations. The Commission has examined the specific deviations sought by the Petitioners in direct correlation with the stakeholder comments received during this process. 17. During the hearing, the Petitioners reiterated that the present Petition has been filed inter alia seeking approval of the deviations proposed in the Tender Documents for long-term procurement of power from the Pump Storage Plants, in terms of Part A, Clause 5.1 of the “Tariff Based Competitive Bidding Guidelines for Procurement of Storage Capacity/ Storage Energy from Pumped Storage Plants” dated 6.2.2025 (“the Guidelines”) issued by the Ministry of Power, Govt. of India. It was further submitted that, in compliance with the Notice dated 7.10.2025 issued by the Commission, the Petitioners have also filed an additional affidavit dated 15.1.2026, placing on record the comments received from various stakeholders, their responses to the stakeholders' queries, deviations from the Guidelines, and the proposed amendments to the Tender Documents. Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the Petitioner, the Commission reserved the matter for order. - _**(f) to adjudicate upon disputes involving generating companies or transmission licensee in regard to matters connected with clauses (a) to (d) above and to refer any dispute for arbitration;**_ 26. The present Petition was first heard on 26.08.2025, wherein the Commission admitted the Petition subject to just exceptions and initially directed the matter to be listed for further hearing on 09.10.2025. Subsequently, to ensure broad stakeholder participation, the Commission issued a Public Notice on 07.10.2025 inviting comments, suggestions, and objections by 17.10.2025 and rescheduled the hearing. Following this, the Petitioners undertook an extensive stakeholder consultation process to ensure that the proposed bidding architecture remained transparent, competitive, and commercially viable for prospective Pump Storage Plant developers. On 15.01.2026, the Petitioners filed an additional affidavit. to bring on record the exhaustive comments and representations received from various industry stakeholders, the Petitioners' detailed responses and the Petitioners’ rebuttals to those queries. imperatives driving the deviations. After giving due consideration to the oral submissions, the documentary evidence, and the statutory provisions, the Commission reserved the matter for its final order. **Proposed Tender Clause (Appendix I & IX):** The Petitioners have proposed that bidders must sign declarations confirming submission of unaudited balance sheets, complete bank statements, and full disclosures of any ongoing litigation prior to signing the agreements. If any submitted documents are found to be misleading, or if the bidder hides pending litigation, or if the bidder withdraws/modifies the bid during the validity period, the Petitioners are empowered to immediately forfeit the Bid Security/PBG, reject the LOA, and explicitly blacklist the bidder and all its affiliates from participating in any future MPPMCL tenders for a strict period of 2 years. 37.
